structure.title: Policies Related to Own Workforce [S1-1]
structure.heading: 13.3.1.1.1 Policies Related to Own Workforce [S1-1]
structure.start_phrase: The Bank operates under labour law regulations alig ned with applicable legislation, ensuring equality before the law and non- discrimination in employment.
structure.summary:
- Scope and focus
  - Social Aspects section (ESRS S1 – Own Workforce) of Bank Pekao S.A. Group’s 2024 report.
  - Bank employees represent 83% of Group headcount; disclosures center on Bank workforce. Non‑employee workers covered by general law; discussed when directly relevant.
  - Double materiality identified workforce impacts (referenced elsewhere in report).

- Governance, policies, and standards
  - HR policies, procedures, and guidelines aligned with national labour law; President of the Management Board oversees implementation via HR Division.
  - Human rights: Code of Conduct as core policy; zero tolerance for trafficking, forced and child labour; commitment to UN Global Compact 10 Principles and UN Guiding Principles (indirectly via the Code).
  - Note on reporting: some MDR elements not fully disclosed as policies predate CSRD/ESRS.

- Employment conditions and stability
  - Work Regulations define rights/obligations for all employees; regularly updated with trade union consultation.
  - Notice periods per Polish law (typically 1–3 months); termination consultations as required.
  - Low turnover (6.9%) and high average tenure (17 years) indicate employment security and satisfaction.

- Working time and flexibility
  - Working hours per Labour Code; monthly schedules; annual leave and parental entitlements communicated.
  - Remote work agreement with trade unions sets rules; flexible arrangements assessed individually; enhanced remote flexibility for parents of children under 8.

- Fair remuneration and governance
  - Remuneration Policy links pay to performance and risk; fixed pay is significant portion; variable pay capped and contingent on thresholds.
  - Market benchmarking and annual implementation report prepared by Nomination & Remuneration Committee; approved by Supervisory Board and presented to GMS.
  - Separate policy for Supervisory Board and Management Board remuneration.

- Social dialogue and freedom of association
  - Multiple internal channels (intranet, chats, forums, town halls); ESG themes emphasized.
  - Constructive relations with trade unions and Works Council; good‑faith negotiations.
  - 2024 trade union engagement: 17 meetings on pay budgets, bonus allocations, ESBF, whistleblowing, anti‑mobbing updates, resilience study, and a Voluntary Redundancy Programme.
  - Supplementary Protocol to Collective Labour Agreement (CLA) on Retail bonus principles signed Oct 23, 2024; registered Nov 18, 2024.

- Collective agreements
  - CLA covers remuneration components and benefits; amendments negotiated with unions and registered with labour inspector.
  - 77% of Bank employees covered by CLA; no collective agreements in subsidiaries.

- Work–life balance and wellbeing
  - Use of part‑time, flexible hours, remote work; investment in mental health, physical activity, and health education.

- Occupational health and safety (OHS)
  - Compliance with national OHS regulations; preventive medicals with specialists.
  - OHS framework: OHS and Fire Protection Rules and Group OHS Policy; overseen by Health & Safety Office under Technology and Operations Division.
  - Digitised occupational risk assessment; introductory and periodic e‑learning; regular first‑aid training; hazard reporting channel; quarterly OHS Committee meetings; intranet resources.

- Diversity, gender equality, and equal pay
  - Gender Equality and Diversity Policy applies to all employees, boards, and key functions; supports inclusion and return‑to‑work after long absences.
  - Recruitment guidelines require gender representation on candidate lists; equal access to development; equal pay principles integrated with Remuneration Policy.
  - 2024 unadjusted gender pay gap: 31.9% (down from 37.9% in 2021); adjusted gap: 2.6%; ongoing monitoring and actions; focus on balanced succession for senior management.
  - Manager training on diversity (Insight Discovery methodology).

- Learning and development
  - Training Policy covers group/individual learning, e‑learning, international programmes, coaching/mentoring, certifications (e.g., CFA, ACCA, CIA), language courses, and postgraduate/MBA support; training agreements govern cost reimbursement where applicable.
  - Key 2024 initiatives:
    - Academy of the Future (future skills).
    - Leadership Academy and Retail Manager Academy (pilot).
    - Managerial Shots: 3 editions, 36 workshops, ~3,500 managers.
    - Development Snacks: 3 editions, 28 workshops, >9,000 participants.
    - Mission: Growth cross‑functional challenge programme (2nd edition).
    - “Without Sugar” women’s programme: 56 activities; tech empowerment; annual gathering (660 participants); Pink October (4,000) and Blue November (2,200) health campaigns; 2nd edition Local Women Leaders programme; total participants >6,600 women (4,000+ in H2).

- Safe and respectful workplace
  - Procedure for counteracting mobbing, discrimination, harassment, and other undesirable behaviour; clear reporting channels; zero tolerance for discrimination across all employment stages.

- Data privacy
  - Employee data protection aligned with broader Bank standards: minimisation, transparency, adequacy, retention, need‑to‑know, privacy by design/default; initial and periodic training for processors.

- Employee voice and cooperation (S1‑2)
  - Annual surveys on engagement/satisfaction, collaboration, and psychophysical wellbeing; anonymous, widely communicated; results cascaded to units and social partners with action plans.
  - 2024 participation: Wellbeing 34%; Collaboration 93%; Engagement 89%; Bank engagement scores in high‑performance zone.
  - Team Climate Survey run in selected teams to assess atmosphere and cooperation.

structure.title: Procedures for Cooperation with Employees and Employee Representatives on Impact Issue [S1-2]
structure.heading: 13.3.1.1.2 Procedures for Cooperation with Employees and Emplo yee Representatives on Impact Issue [S1-2]
structure.start_phrase: The organisational culture we foster is based on co llaboration, openness to diversity, and adherence t o the Bank’s values.
structure.summary:
- Highlights extensive development and inclusion initiatives, especially for women: technology education programs (“Closer to Technology,” “emPower Women”), an annual women’s event with 660 participants, two employee health-awareness campaigns (Pink October: 4,000; Blue November: 2,200), and the 2nd Development Program for Local Women Leaders; over 6,600 women engaged in 2024 (4,000+ in H2).
- Details measures to prevent workplace violence and harassment, including a formal Procedure for Counteracting Mobbing, Discrimination, Harassment, or Other Undesirable Behaviour, zero-tolerance for discrimination, and dedicated reporting channels.
- Outlines employee privacy safeguards: data minimisation, transparency, adequacy, retention policies, need-to-know access, privacy by design/default, supported by procedures and regular training.
- Describes employee engagement and dialogue processes: annual psychophysical well-being, collaboration, and engagement/satisfaction surveys; anonymous participation; broad internal communication; results cascaded to management, Works Council, and unions; unit-level action plans.
- Provides 2024 survey metrics: Well-being (15 Jul–15 Aug, 34% participation), Collaboration (29 Aug–19 Sep, 93%), Engagement/Satisfaction (22 Oct–13 Nov, 89%); overall engagement in the market’s high-performance zone.
- Mentions additional feedback tools: Team Climate Survey for selected teams and exit interviews to inform retention strategies; World Values Day event with 300+ attendees.
- Confirms robust employee representation: nine trade unions with 53.8% membership (as of 31 Dec 2024), union access to intranet communications, and an active Works Council per national legislation.
- Explains negative impact mitigation and reporting: whistleblowing and anti-mobbing procedures define internal channels and response steps; notes no systematic assessment yet of employee trust or channel effectiveness; employees must acknowledge understanding.
- Addresses AI-driven transformation risks to job security in customer service roles (branches, business/corporate/private banking centres, call centres) and outlines upskilling focus as mitigation.
- Presents the Academy of the Future program to build future competencies (cognitive and technological, including AI), with webinars/workshops/materials; Q4 2024 webinars covered AI, quantum finance, cognitive resilience/agility, strategic prospecting, and purpose-driven work; next edition slated for late 2024/early 2025.

structure.title: Processes for Addressing Negative Impacts and Employee Reporting Channels [S1-3]
structure.heading: 13.3.1.1.3 Processes for Addressing Negative Impacts and Emplo yee Reporting Channels [S1-3]
structure.start_phrase: We respect employees’ rights to freedom of associat ion as well as their rights to information and cons ultation.
structure.summary:
- Focus on employee engagement and feedback: confidential engagement surveys used to improve team operations; exit interviews and questionnaires analyzed to inform retention strategies.
- Cultural alignment initiatives: World Values Day held for the second time, a full-day event with workshops and inspirational sessions; over 300 attendees, more than half from the sales network.
- Employee representation and social dialogue: nine trade union organizations with 53.8% union membership (as of 31 Dec 2024); unions represent all employees in collective matters and have intranet access to communicate updates; Works Council functions under the Act of 7 April 2006 for information and consultation.
- Grievance and ethics mechanisms: formal procedures for counteracting mobbing, discrimination, harassment, and other undesirable behavior, as well as a whistleblowing procedure detailing internal reporting channels and response actions; all employees must acknowledge understanding. The Bank has not yet systematically assessed employee trust in, or the effectiveness of, these channels.
- Managing material impacts from digitalization/AI: recognition that AI, automation, and robotics may displace roles, particularly in customer service (branches, business/corporate/private banking outlets, and especially call centers), affecting both employment and civil law contract workers with customer-service-centric skills.
- Mitigation through reskilling and future competencies: HR policy prioritizes skills development, notably via the Academy of the Future—webinars, workshops, and learning materials covering cognitive and technological competencies, including AI. In Q4 2024, five webinars addressed AI, quantum finance, cognitive resilience and agility, strategic prospecting, and purpose-driven work; the third edition of the program is scheduled for late 2024/early 2025.

  - Internal reporting channels described; employees must acknowledge procedures.
  - No formal, systematic assessments yet of employee trust in reporting channels or their effectiveness.

- Managing material workforce impacts from AI/digitalization:
  - Automation and AI pose job security risks, especially for customer service roles (branches, centers, call centers).
  - Mitigation via upskilling/reskilling:
    - Academy of the Future: webinars/workshops on AI, quantum finance, cognitive agility, strategic prospecting, purpose; new edition at 2024/2025 turn.

structure.title: Policies Related to Consumers and End-Users [S4-1]
structure.heading: 13.3.2.1.1 Policies Related to Consumers and End-Users [S4-1]
structure.start_phrase: As part of our double materiality assessment, we as ked ourselves which aspects of our operations impac t our customers, both positively and negatively.
structure.summary:
- Scope and approach: The Bank frames customer relationships around trust, ethics, fairness, and professionalism, with a focus on inclusivity for children, youth, seniors, and people with disabilities. A double materiality assessment identified six priority areas: non-discrimination, access to information, access to products, personal and financial security, consumer privacy/data protection, and responsible marketing.

- Governance and standards: Operations are anchored in the Pekao Group Code of Conduct, ensuring ethical conduct and alignment with best practices. Policies and processes are designed to prevent misselling, support financial stability, and safeguard customer interests.

- Non-discrimination and accessibility: The Bank prohibits any discrimination or harassment and promotes inclusive, easy-to-understand communication. Tailored solutions include senior guidance, youth products (e.g., PeoPay Kids with parental controls and educational features), and clear, age-appropriate data notices for minors. In September 2024, the “Pekao Without Barriers” programme was launched to meet the 2025 accessibility law, focusing on removing service barriers, upgrading branches (including 12 modernised sites), and ensuring physical accessibility standards.

- Access to information and consumer protection: The Bank commits to accurate, complete disclosures and avoidance of unfair practices. Contract templates and APR calculations align with the Consumer Credit Act to mitigate “free credit sanction” risks; common dispute areas are noted, and the Bank will monitor impacts of the CJEU’s 13 Feb 2025 ruling (C‑472/23). Customer insights are informed by external research. MiFID processes include profiling, target market checks, risk warnings, annual reviews, and defined internal governance for brokerage activities.

- Access to products and product governance: Product development emphasizes ethics, transparency, and suitability. In 2024, about 1,000 more employees were certified to offer investment funds, broadening access to Pekao TFI products. A formal New Product Introduction Policy requires Management Board approval, ESG alignment, customer impact testing, comprehensive risk assessments, and compliance (including FATCA/CRS). EBA-guided product testing and stress tests are applied. A new Customer Experience Management Model (2024) advances omnichannel, digitization, personalization, AI/data use, and trust-building.

- Personal and financial security: The Bank enhanced anti-fraud capabilities in 2024 via customer education, advanced transaction monitoring, stronger platform controls (instant blocking, two-factor authentication including hardware keys), and increased analyst staffing. Internal rules were updated in line with the competition authority’s stance on unauthorised transactions.

- Consumer privacy and data protection: GDPR compliance is central, with strict adherence to lawfulness, transparency, purpose limitation, data minimisation, integrity, and confidentiality. Extensive internal regulations govern data handling, breach response, authorizations, retention, and outsourcing. Responsibilities are defined across the Management Board, unit directors, and employees, with mandatory training and DPO oversight of processes, contracts, and new technologies in partnership with the Security Centre.

- Responsible marketing: The Bank’s Rules for Creating Marketing Communications ensure legal compliance, ethical standards, non-discrimination, and accurate risk representation. Marketing to customers over 69 is not actively pursued; all materials are reviewed by Compliance. Investment marketing must clearly state risks (including potential capital loss) with equal prominence to benefits and is targeted only to customers within the MiFID-defined target market.

- Financial education: The Bank runs education initiatives on budgeting, saving, investing, safe use of banking apps, and financial risks, often via social partners and employee volunteering, guided by internal regulations and tailored to local community needs.

- Engagement processes [S4-2]: The Bank emphasizes compliance with laws and internal rules, cultivating a shared responsibility culture among employees for proper process execution and continuous improvement in customer satisfaction.

- Data protection and GDPR compliance: The Data Protection Officer and related units review new processes, projects, regulations, contracts, and technologies to ensure GDPR compliance and high personal data security. Clear channels are provided for reporting personal data breaches.
- Responsible marketing: Strict Rules for Creating Marketing Communications ensure legal compliance, ethical standards, non-discrimination, and transparent risk disclosure (including investment risks with equal prominence to benefits). Marketing is aligned to MiFID-defined target groups and is not actively directed to customers over 69. All materials are reviewed by Compliance.
- Financial education: Programs, workshops, and campaigns (often via employee volunteering and the “We are Close” grant program) boost public and customer financial literacy, tailored to local community needs.
- Consumer engagement and customer experience: A bank-wide customer experience model guides improvements across segments. The bank expands research and feedback collection (including Google Business Profile), monitors service interactions (security, clarity, suitability), and trains advisors, showing steady service quality gains.
- Plain language and quality of communication: Standardized document layouts, expanded plain-language consultant network, staff training, a “Prosto po polsku” knowledge hub, legal design adoption, and participation in the Polish Bank Association’s working group drive clearer, simpler customer communications.
- Innovation and digital transformation: The Innovation Lab advances solutions through design thinking, service design, and lean startup, focusing on innovation design, customer research, partnerships, and culture. 2024 initiatives included ESG tools, micro-enterprise tech, investment/insurance concepts, and a parental control panel for children’s banking. The Innovation Factory refines ideas via iterative customer studies. A pilot carbon footprint calculator for business customers (32 participants) progressed toward service integration.
- Market research and brand tracking: Ongoing qualitative and quantitative studies refine products, communications, and customer journeys; internal education shares insights on youth, seniors, and at-risk groups. Brand awareness remains high (Q3 2024: 2nd in Top of Mind among 18–64; strong rankings among youth and SMEs). Dedicated research informs Premium segment offer development.
- Complaints and remediation processes: A formal Complaint Handling Process ensures legality, transparency, clarity, and timeliness. Multiple channels are available (branch, helpline, online, e-Delivery), with options for representation, appeals, ombudsman and regulator escalation. GDPR safeguards (including encryption) apply. 2024 saw 205,803 complaints in retail/private/JDG; Q4 channel use was mainly digital (PeoPay 36%, Pekao24 18%), helpline 29%, branch 15%. Post-complaint NPS improved to 0 in Q4 (+13 points QoQ).

structure.heading: 13.3.2.1.3 Processes for Addressing Negative Impacts and Consu mer and End-User Complaint Channels [S4 -3]
structure.start_phrase: We prioritise open communication and collaboration, offering multiple channels for customers to provid e feedback and submit complaints.
structure.summary:
- Focus areas: customer complaint handling, personal data breach reporting, and actions to manage material consumer impacts and risks (notably cybersecurity and fraud).
- Complaint handling framework: governed by Bank Pekao’s Complaint Handling Process; aligned with the Act on Complaints Handling by Financial Market Entities and GDPR; principles of legality, transparency, clarity, and timely resolution.
- Accessible channels: complaints can be filed in-branch, in writing, via helpline, online banking, or e-Delivery; policy details shared at agreement signing and on the website.
- Representation and processing rules: authorised representatives accepted with explicit banking secrecy waiver; anonymous complaints not processed.
- Escalation paths: Customer Ombudsman for complex cases; out-of-court resolution via Banking Ombudsman (Polish Bank Association) or Financial Ombudsman; appeals possible via the same channels and to the Management Board, Supervisory Board, KNF, and local consumer protection offices.
- Data protection in complaints: strict confidentiality; encrypted data transmissions with separate password channel; ongoing satisfaction monitoring and quarterly surveys.
- 2024 complaint metrics: 205,803 complaints in retail, private banking, and sole proprietorship segments; Q4 channel usage—PeoPay 36%, Pekao24 18%, helpline 29%, branches 15%; post-complaint NPS improved to 0 (+13 points), with 36% promoters and 36% detractors.
- Personal data breach reporting: via helpline, branch, writing, email (iod@pekao.com.pl), or online banking; DPO maintains registers of reports, incidents, and UODO complaints; responses within GDPR deadlines; majority of correspondence electronic; no complaints about non-response; privacy clause embedded across processes and employee policies.
- Consumer protection actions: continuous threat assessment, sector information exchange, and education via campaigns, website, and social media to build cyber awareness and resilience.
- Marketing and product controls: all customer-facing materials reviewed by Legal and Compliance; New Product Implementation Process ensures compliant customer documentation and adherence to appropriate banking practices.
- 2024 security enhancements: automated PESEL restriction checks block new agreements and cash withdrawals above three times minimum wage when a PESEL is flagged; overseen by the VP for Retail Banking.
- Telephone security and service: digital business cards in mobile apps for verifying employees and customers; centralized branch contact number; replacement of landlines with recorded mobile phones to counter spoofing; educational video on bank-impersonation fraud.
- Cyber education framework: “Security Education” policy guides initiatives; #CYBERczujni (#CYBERAware) campaign with reach and engagement tracking.
- Financial resilience products: promotion of CPI PEX, CPI KH, Life Insurance, and Property Insurance; product quality monitored via complaints, claim rejection rates, and loss ratios in cooperation with insurers.

structure.title: Actions Taken Regarding Material Impacts on Consumers and End-Users and Approaches to Managing Material Risks and Leveraging Material Opportunities Related to Consumers and End-Users, as well as the Effectiveness of Such Actions [S4-4]
structure.heading: 13.3.2.1.4 Actions Taken Regarding Material Impacts on Consume rs and End-Users and Approaches to Managing Material Risks and Leveraging Material Opportunities Related to Consumers and End- Users, as well as the Effectiveness of Such Actions [S4-4]
structure.start_phrase: We implement a range of measures to prevent materia l negative impacts on our customers’ financial secu rity and safety.
structure.summary:
- Describes customer data protection governance: multiple breach-reporting channels, Data Protection Officer oversight, GDPR-compliant response timelines, and privacy information embedded across customer and employee processes.
- Details actions to prevent material negative impacts on consumers, with emphasis on cybersecurity threat assessment, sector information-sharing, and ongoing education via website and social media.
- Ensures customer communications and product launches avoid misleading information through Legal and Compliance reviews and a regulated New Product Implementation Process.
- Introduces 2024 security enhancements:
  - Automated PESEL restriction checks that block new agreements and large cash withdrawals to mitigate identity theft, overseen by the VP for Retail Banking.
  - Digital business cards in mobile apps to verify bank employees and securely identify customers.
  - Centralized branch phone number, remote resolution focus, removal of landlines, and recorded mobile calls to counter spoofing; complemented by an educational anti-fraud video.
- Outlines continuous security education under the Bank’s Security Education policy and the #CYBERczujni campaign, monitored for reach and engagement.
- Highlights promotion of insurance (CPI PEX, CPI KH, life, property) to support customer financial resilience, with rigorous monitoring of complaints, claim rejections, and loss ratios, and close cooperation with insurers.
- Reports implementation of Recommendation U and CPI best practices in 2024, improving product quality, loss ratios, and claim acceptance, and enhancing needs-based product matching.
- Covers personal data protection processes: notifying data subjects about breaches with mitigation guidance, informing them about data processing (including BIK), and analyzing feedback from the Polish DPA (UODO).
- Explains effectiveness assessment via UODO feedback on reported incidents and complaints, with DPO review of awareness communications.
- Notes that initiatives require significant resources, though detailed initiative-level financials are not currently feasible.
- Presents strategy-setting and targets: multi-year strategic planning based on macro and sector analyses, risk profile, and SWOT; ESG Strategy 2021–2024 (Pillar 2) priorities include equal opportunity, preventing social exclusion, financial access, customer satisfaction, digitalization, and reputation strengthening.
- States customer insights (surveys, complaints, brand studies) inform objectives, though customers are not directly involved in planning.
- 2024 progress highlights: improved service accessibility for people with special needs and ongoing reputation monitoring, with prior surveys confirming strong brand reputation.

structure.title: Goals for Managing Material Negative Impacts, Increasing Positive Impacts, and Managing Material Risks and Opportunities [S4-5]
structure.heading: 13.3.2.2.1 Goals for Managing Material Negative Impacts, Incre asing Positive Impacts, and Managing Material Risks and Opportunities [S4-5]
structure.start_phrase: Strategic goals, including those that relate to act ivities carried out towards customers, are set as p art of the strategic planning process.
structure.summary:
- Implementation of Recommendation U and alignment with Best Practices for CPI Insurance, resulting in higher-quality, more tailored insurance products, improved loss ratios, and lower claim rejection rates.
- Strengthened customer/consumer risk management with a focus on personal data protection: proactive notification to Data Subjects about breaches, guidance on mitigating consequences, and transparent information on data processing (including by BIK).
- Ongoing analysis of feedback from the Polish Data Protection Office (UODO) on reported data breaches and Data Subject complaints as the primary effectiveness metric for privacy initiatives.
- Customer fraud-prevention awareness campaigns (e.g., phishing, online scams), with DPO oversight of all customer communications.
- Note that initiatives require significant resources, but detailed financial breakdowns per initiative are not currently feasible.
- Metrics and Targets (ESRS S4-5): strategic goal-setting via a comprehensive planning process (macroeconomic assumptions, sector trends, SWOT, risk assessments, review of prior strategy outcomes) involving all major units.
- ESG Strategy 2021–2024, Pillar 2: Social Responsibility—priorities include equal opportunity, preventing social exclusion, expanding financial access, boosting customer satisfaction, digitalization, and brand reputation; customer insights from surveys and complaints inform objectives.
- 2024 achievements:
  - Accessibility: continued removal of barriers for customers with special needs.
  - Reputation: strong standing among Polish banks on trust, stability, and security (Q3 2024), monitored via long-running GfK Polonia studies; ongoing tracking of awareness, consideration, conversion, and perception.
  - Customer satisfaction: NPS improvements—individuals +3 pts (Q4 2024 vs Q4 2023), sole proprietors (JDG) +14 pts (2024 vs 2023), SME +3 pts, MID +15 pts; targets set in 2022, monitored via external benchmarks and bank-run surveys.
  - Digitalization: continued growth of digital channels, mobile payments, and remote services for easy access.
  - Education: programs supporting financial literacy and equalizing opportunities for at-risk groups (children, youth, seniors, local communities).
  - Periodic public reporting of strategic goal progress on the bank’s website.
- Corporate Governance Information (ESRS G1):
  - Corporate culture anchored in four values: #prosto (straightforward), #razem (together), #odważnie (boldly), #odpowiedzialnie (responsibly); ESG Strategy as the governance framework for ethics and responsibility.
  - Mandatory training (onboarding and ongoing) in corporate governance, ethics/Code of Conduct, whistleblowing, anti-corruption, and compliance; 1,151 employees completed Code of Conduct training in 2024.
  - Annual Management Board review of adherence to the Pekao Group Code of Conduct; principles include legal compliance, continuous improvement, transparent, trust-based client relationships, and strong risk culture.
  - Code of Conduct accessible internally and publicly; adoption of the Polish Bank Association’s Banking Ethics Code as a sectoral standard guiding ethical practices and reinforcing trust and reputation.

structure.title: Business Conduct Policies and Corporate Culture [G1-1]
structure.heading: 13.4.1.2.1 Business Conduct Policies and Corporate Culture [G1 -1]
structure.start_phrase: A key element of our operations is the development of a stable organisational culture.
structure.summary:
- Scope and framing: Corporate Governance Information under ESRS G1, with the detailed roles and expertise of administrative, supervisory, and management bodies referenced to another section (13.1.2.1).

- Corporate culture and ethics:
  - Four core values defined in 2021 (#prosto/straightforward, #razem/together, #odważnie/boldly, #odpowiedzialnie/responsibly) guide behavior and engagement.
  - ESG Strategy acts as the overarching governance framework for integrating ethics and social responsibility.
  - Mandatory training for staff on corporate governance, ethics/Code of Conduct, whistleblowing, anti-corruption, and compliance; embedded in onboarding.
  - Annual review of Code of Conduct adherence by the Management Board; 1,151 employees completed Code of Conduct training in 2024.
  - Code of Conduct accessible on intranet and public website.

- Sector ethics alignment:
  - Adoption of the Banking Ethics Code of the Polish Bank Association; active participation in the Association’s Banking Ethics Committee.
  - Code covers general principles, client relations, employee relations, interbank/partner relations, responsible banking, and innovation/technology.

- Whistleblowing and anti-mobbing framework:
  - Bank (83% of Group workforce) sets Group standards; other entities align with Bank policies.
  - Two core documents: Anti-Mobbing Procedure and Whistleblowing Procedure; the latter updated on 25 Sept 2024 to align with the Whistleblower Protection Act.
  - Anti-Mobbing Procedure: formal complaint process, appointed commission review, proportional disciplinary measures, preference for amicable resolution, strict anti-retaliation provisions.
  - Whistleblowing Procedure: broad eligibility (employees, contractors, shareholders, board members, interns, volunteers, suppliers’ staff, pre-/post-contract individuals, union board members); anonymous or named reporting via email, post (including to Supervisory Board chair for reports on Management Board), recorded phone line, and in-person meetings (scheduled within 14 days).
  - Investigation process yields a final report approved by the designated Management Board Member, with corrective/disciplinary and preventive actions.
  - Protections: consideration of all reports, confidentiality, impartial and timely verification, acknowledgment and outcome feedback; protections extend to helpers and connected persons.
  - Incentives/support for whistleblowers: psychological support, temporary reassignment, remote work, paid leave, and transfers where justified.
  - Training: mandatory familiarization within three months for new employees; internal communications; new e-learning in development; process handlers use public trainings; procedures published for non-employees with data appendices.
  - Objective emphasizes ethical, compliant environment rather than measurable sustainability targets.

- CSRD-related disclosure approach:
  - For MDR-P: presents policy content, scope, stakeholder considerations, accessibility, and responsible units; does not list external standards/initiatives.
  - For MDR-T: discloses scope and base period but lacks measurability, methodology/science basis, stakeholder involvement, milestones, and performance tracking.

- Supplier relationship management:
  - Commitment to long-term, trust-based, equal treatment of suppliers; compliance with procedures, best practices, and Polish law.
  - Procurement governed by three core internal regulations; regular reviews; Dec 2024 update adds ESG factors and anti-greenwashing provisions, without setting measurable sustainability objectives.
  - Uniform contract scopes, open invitations to qualified bidders, transparent communication of outcomes.
  - ESG Questionnaire: previously required above PLN 1m net; since Dec 2024 mandatory for all suppliers and contract values, across all enterprise sizes; focuses on environmental and human rights compliance; positioned as mitigating value chain risks in these areas.
  - Supplier Code of Ethics (2023): integrated into procurement; promotes Bank values and sets responsible, transparent, ESG-aligned expectations for suppliers and subcontractors.
  - Environmental criteria in the Code include valid permits/licences, timely environmental fees, and compliance with environmental reporting (the excerpt indicates further criteria continue).

structure.title: Supplier Relationship Management [G1-2]
structure.heading: 13.4.1.2.2 Supplier Relationship Management [G1-2]
structure.start_phrase: We place great importance on partnership-based rela tionships with our suppliers, regardless of the siz e of their businesses.
structure.summary:
- Emphasis on ethics and compliance: The Whistleblowing Procedure and broader governance policies aim to ensure transparency, ethics, and legal compliance rather than quantified sustainability targets. Disclosures under CSRD minimum requirements are limited to descriptions of policies and targets; there are no disclosed metrics, methodologies, milestones, stakeholder input, or performance tracking.
- Supplier relationship management: Procurement is conducted fairly and uniformly under three core regulations. A December 2024 update to the Procurement Policy incorporated ESG factors and anti-greenwashing provisions. All suppliers, regardless of size or contract value, must now complete an ESG Questionnaire (previously required only for contracts over PLN 1 million), covering environmental and human rights compliance; completion is mandatory for participation.
- Supplier Code of Ethics (2023): Defines ESG expectations for suppliers across environmental (permits, reporting, emissions reduction and transparency, waste and resource management), social (prohibitions on forced/child labor and discrimination, fair pay, freedom of association, OHS), and corporate governance (anti-corruption, AML/CFT, consumer and data protection, antitrust, fair competition, IP/confidentiality, conflicts of interest) areas. The Code is a guiding document; the ESG Questionnaire/Form is used for verification. The Procurement Department manages it; external stakeholders were not involved; relevant sections are public. The approach is intended to help manage climate-related risks, including Scope 3 emissions.
- Tax transparency: The Bank collaborates with tax authorities under CRS and FATCA, with internal procedures guiding customer due diligence, classification, and reporting to the National Tax Administration, particularly for front-line and Tax Department staff.
- Cybersecurity and data security: The Bank Security Centre (CBB) oversees the ICT Security Strategy, Information Security Policy, and related documentation, aligned with legal and supervisory requirements. Policies apply to all employees and are communicated internally; there are no CSRD-aligned targets or metrics.
- Anti-corruption and bribery: Zero tolerance for corruption, bribery, and facilitation payments, with protections for employees who refuse or report. The Anti-Corruption Policy, approved by the Management Board and accessible internally, includes a programme addressing risk controls in gifts and entertainment, intermediaries, contractor relations, recruitment, donations and sponsorships, and participation in public procurement.

structure.title: Preventing and Detecting Corruption and Bribery [G1-3]
structure.heading: 13.4.1.2.3 Preventing and Detecting Corruption and Bribery [G1 -3]
structure.start_phrase: Within the Pekao Group, we take a zero-tolerance ap proach to corruption and bribery, including any cir cumstances that could facilitate corrupt practices.
structure.summary:
- Tax transparency: The Bank supports international efforts against tax avoidance and money laundering by complying with CRS and FATCA. Internal orders define responsibilities for customer due diligence, collection of declarations, client FATCA/CRS classification, and reporting to the Head of the National Tax Administration, primarily by frontline staff and the Tax Department.

- Cybersecurity and data security: Focus on strengthening confidentiality, integrity, availability, and authenticity of data; supporting organisational resilience; and raising employee awareness. The Bank Security Centre (CBB) leads cybersecurity, implements the ICT Security Strategy, and oversees the Information Security Policy and related regulations aligned with legal and supervisory requirements. Policies apply to all employees, with targeted rules for specific groups and communicated updates. No CSRD-aligned targets or metrics are set in this area.

- Anti-corruption and bribery prevention: Zero-tolerance stance covering employees and third parties; protection for those refusing participation or reporting. The Management Board-approved Anti-Corruption Policy governs prevention, risk identification, and procedures, and embeds an Anti-Corruption Programme addressing gifts and entertainment, intermediaries, contractors, recruitment, donations and sponsorships, public procurement, M&A, and major investments. Controls are designed, supervised, and monitored independently; risks are assessed within the Compliance Risk Management framework; secure channels enable open or confidential reporting; and accurate, transparent record-keeping is mandated. Quarterly reporting to the Management Board is performed.

- Governance and roles: An independent Anti-Corruption Officer within the Compliance Department analyzes reports, issues risk-management recommendations, and has information-access rights. Reports are logged in a central IT system. Identification of incidents is separated from investigation (conducted by the Officer or Security Centre).

- Training: Standardized anti-corruption e-learning for all employees (12,869 trained). Onboarding for new hires; annual refreshers for risk roles and Management Board; biennial for others; plans to include Supervisory Board. Tailored trainings are offered as needed.

- Resources: Anti-corruption resources include Officer remuneration, IT systems for reporting, and training costs; these are embedded in broader operating expenses. No changes to resource levels are planned.

- 2024 metrics and incidents: No criminal proceedings for corruption/bribery; one unsuccessful bribery attempt; no employee dismissals or sanctions recorded; no partner contracts terminated or not renewed due to corruption/bribery; fines amounted to PLN 0.

structure.title: Corruption or Bribery Incidents [G1-4]
structure.heading: 13.4.1.3.1 Corruption or Bribery Incidents [G1-4]
structure.start_phrase: In 2024, no criminal proceedings were identified co ncerning corruption or bribery-related offences com mitted by own workforce.
structure.summary:
- Focus: Bank Pekao S.A. Group’s 2024 activities in anti-corruption, payment practices, and tax transparency, including metrics and controls.

- Anti-corruption program:
  - Comprehensive internal regulations, ongoing monitoring, and a standardized training program.
  - 12,869 employees trained; 100% of roles considered potentially exposed to corruption/bribery risks.
  - Training topics include definitions and risk management, intermediaries, gifts/entertainment, recruitment, contractors, donations/sponsorships, M&A and major investments, public procurement, procedures for public authority investigations, criminal liability, standards/best practices, and a knowledge test.
  - Delivery: one-time e-learning at onboarding; annual training for risk roles and Management Board; biennial for others; plan to extend to Supervisory Board; ad hoc tailored sessions as needed.
  - Resources cover Anti-Corruption Officer remuneration, IT systems for report processing, and training costs; precise amounts not isolated; no planned change in funding levels.

- Metrics and targets:
  - Corruption/bribery incidents (G1-4): No criminal proceedings identified in 2024; one unsuccessful bribery attempt; no dismissals/punishments recorded; no partner contracts terminated/not renewed due to corruption; no fines (PLN 0).
  - Payment practices (G1-6): No unified Group payment policy; adherence to supplier contract terms. Average invoice processing time in 2024 was 17.92 days; key subsidiaries: 14 days at Pekao Faktoring; Pekao Leasing pays per invoice due date. One legal proceeding on delayed lease rent payment (first-instance court).
  - Tax transparency: Compliance with Polish regulation implementing international tax information exchange (FATCA/CRS).
    - Processes: customer onboarding with FATCA/CRS declarations; IT systems for identification, online submissions/updates; customer classification; system enhancements for reporting (IFT app with Residency/FATCA/CRS modules); monitoring of status changes; annual high-balance reviews; customer communication campaigns; internal control testing; annual reporting to the National Revenue Administration by 30 June.
    - Objectives: timely FAT-1/CRS-1 submissions; quarterly outreach to customers with potential classification changes/missing data; annual high-balance reviews; execution of the internal control plan.
    - Effectiveness monitoring: annual FATCA/CRS testing within the Internal Control System (results in Compeo; semi-annual reporting to the VP, Financial Division); periodic Internal Audit (latest FATCA audit Q1 2024, CRS Q3 2022; all recommendations implemented; ongoing monitoring in Gaudi); maintenance of a Register of Due Diligence Activities for customer classification.

structure.title: Payment Practices [G1-6]
structure.heading: 13.4.1.3.2 Payment Practices [G1-6]
structure.start_phrase: Favourable commercial terms, timely payments, and t ransparent, fair business relationships are our top priorities.
structure.summary:
- Scope: 2024 Bank Pekao S.A. Group report excerpt covering Payment Practices [G1-6] and Tax Transparency.

- Payment Practices:
  - Emphasis on fair, transparent relationships and timely payments; no formal, unified Group-wide payment policy—terms follow individual supplier contracts.
  - Average invoice processing time in 2024: 17.92 days (Group IT system data).
  - Subsidiaries: Pekao Faktoring Sp. z o.o. averages 14 days; Pekao Leasing Sp. z o.o. pays per invoice due date.
  - One legal case in 2024 concerning delayed lease rent payment; in first-instance court.

- Tax Transparency:
  - Compliance aligned with Poland’s regulation on international tax information exchange (FATCA/CRS).
  - Key activities:
    - Customer onboarding with FATCA/CRS declarations.
    - IT systems for identification, onboarding, online declaration submission/updates.
    - Customer classification using declarations and personal/contact data.
    - Enhanced IT for data reporting to the Head of National Revenue Administration via IFT (Residency, FATCA, CRS modules).
    - Ongoing monitoring of changes affecting classification.
    - Annual high-balance customer reviews.
    - Targeted customer communications to resolve data gaps/discrepancies.
    - Internal control tests sampling FATCA/CRS compliance.
    - Annual data reporting by 30 June for the prior fiscal year.
  - Objectives:
    - Timely FAT-1/CRS-1 submissions by 30 June.
    - Quarterly communications to customers with potential classification changes or missing data.
    - Annual reviews of high-balance customers.
    - Execution of an internal control plan with audits completed on schedule.
  - Monitoring and effectiveness:
    - Internal Control System with annual FATCA/CRS testing; results stored in Compeo and reported semi-annually to the VP overseeing the Financial Division.
    - Periodic Internal Audit reviews (latest: FATCA Q1 2024; CRS Q3 2022); recommendations implemented; ongoing monitoring via Gaudi tool.
    - Register of Due Diligence Activities documenting all customer-level due diligence within the IFT-Residency classification system.

structure.title: Tax Transparency
structure.heading: 13.4.1.3.3 Tax Transparency
structure.start_phrase: Tax transparency activities are carried out in line with the Regulation on the Implementation of Certa in Obligations Arising from Tax Information Exchange Laws Between the Republic of Poland and Other Countries.
structure.summary:
- Payment practices: Emphasis on fair, transparent relationships and timely settlements; no unified Group-wide payment policy, adherence to contract terms. Average 2024 invoice processing time: 17.92 days (Group); Pekao Faktoring: 14 days; Pekao Leasing: pays per invoice due date. One ongoing first-instance legal case regarding delayed lease rent payment.
- Tax transparency: Full FATCA/CRS compliance framework covering onboarding, customer classification, IT systems for identification and reporting (IFT), monitoring changes, annual high-balance reviews, communication campaigns, internal control testing, and annual reporting to the Head of the National Revenue Administration by 30 June. Objectives include on-time FAT-1/CRS-1 submissions, quarterly outreach to customers with potential data changes, annual reviews, and execution of an internal control plan. Effectiveness monitored via: Internal Control System testing (Compeo), Internal Audit reviews (FATCA audit Q1 2024, CRS audit Q3 2022; recommendations implemented, tracked in Gaudi), a Due Diligence Register (IFT-Residency), data quality indicators in the Data Governance Platform (PZD), and official UPO confirmations.
- Cybersecurity and data security: CBB executes the ICT Security Strategy to raise security levels and strengthen the ICT environment through employee/customer education (cyberPEKAO, awareness campaigns, ZBP initiatives), broad internal/external communications, and partnerships (e.g., CyberDefence24). Key projects: vulnerability scanner replacement, cloud data/app security, database protection, advanced testing tools. Tools rolled out mid-2022 to various quarters of 2023; all completed by end-2024. Continuous risk monitoring, regular policy reviews, and periodic security reporting to Management Board and Supervisory bodies. Compliance assessed under Poland’s National Cybersecurity System Act and reinforced through internal controls.
- Contact information: Sustainability data contributors include Bank Pekao and key subsidiaries (e.g., Pekao Bank Hipoteczny, Pekao Faktoring, Pekao Leasing, Pekao Investment entities). Report contacts: Financial Planning Department representatives; email: esg@pekao.com.pl.

structure.title: Cybersecurity (and data security)
structure.heading: 13.4.1.3.4 Cybersecurity (and data security)
structure.start_phrase: The projects undertaken by the CBB as part of cyber security and data security efforts are aligned with the ICT Security Strategy at Bank Pekao S.A.
structure.summary:
- Data governance for regulatory reporting: quality indicators within the Data Governance Platform (PZD) to ensure FATCA/CRS data completeness and quality, plus official submission confirmations (UPO) for FAT-1/CRS-1 reports.
- Cybersecurity and data security: CBB initiatives aligned with the Bank’s ICT Security Strategy to raise information security and strengthen the ICT environment through security solutions and education for employees and customers.
- Awareness and communication: cyberPEKAO training and customer webinars; #StayCYBERaware and CRM campaigns; participation in the Polish Bank Association’s “Do Not Help Thieves” campaign; internal (security portal, bulletins, alerts) and external (website, social media, app, radio) communications; collaboration with CyberDefence24; funded via Capex and Opex.
- Key security projects: vulnerability scanner replacement; cloud data/application security; database protection; advanced testing tools. Projects followed risk and market analyses; advanced testing tools launched mid-2022, others in 2023; all completed by end-2024, mitigating emerging risks with ongoing monitoring.
- Oversight and compliance: regular reviews of information security documents within the Information Security Policy; quarterly and annual ICT security reports to the Management Board, Supervisory Board’s Risk Committee, and Supervisory Board; cybersecurity maturity assessments under the Act on the National Cybersecurity System; internal security controls to enhance effectiveness and data protection.
- Contact and scope: sustainability-related 2024 data sourced from Bank Pekao and key subsidiaries (e.g., Pekao Bank Hipoteczny, Pekao Leasing, Pekao Investment Management/TFI, etc.). Inquiries directed to named Financial Planning Department representatives via esg@pekao.com.pl.
